outcomes.original: Filing step: Secure the entity formation, EIN, seller's permit, and San Francisco business registration certificate. What to say: Form the legal entity with the California Secretary of State (LLC or corporation), obtain the federal EIN online from the IRS, register for the California seller's permit with CDTFA, and file for the San Francisco business registration certificate with the Treasurer & Tax Collector. ABC will not process the license transfer until the entity, EIN, seller's permit, and lease are in place. The business registration certificate generates the Business Account Number (BAN) that every other city department requires.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File the Conditional Use Authorization application with San Francisco Planning Department, requesting authorization to intensify the existing restaurant use by upgrading from Type 41 to Type 47 on-sale general license. What to say: Frame the application as intensification of an existing legally permitted restaurant use under Planning Code § 178, citing the 1987 CUA (Motion No. 13556, Case No. 1986.553C) that previously authorized a Type 47 license at this address. Emphasize that the restaurant has operated continuously since 1986 with no interruption or abandonment, that the space will not be enlarged, that no construction or change of use is proposed, and that the applicant will maintain the restaurant as a bona fide eating place with at least 51% of gross receipts from food sales. Submit a business plan showing that meal service is primary and alcohol service is incidental. Pre-application meeting with the Planning staff is recommended to confirm the scope and to determine whether the 1987, 1998, and 2010 CUA conditions will carry forward or be superseded.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Identify and enter escrow for a Type 47 license through a California ABC license broker, with the purchase agreement contingent on CUA approval and ABC transfer approval. What to say: Type 47 is a quota license; new licenses are not issued by ABC in San Francisco County, so the license must be purchased on the open market and transferred to the premises. Engage an ABC license broker to locate an available Type 47 license (expect $100,000 to $450,000 in San Francisco). The escrow period is typically 90 to 180 days. Make the lease and the license purchase contingent on Planning's CUA approval and ABC's transfer approval, including any public convenience or necessity finding required for the undue-concentration census tract.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File the ABC Type 47 premises-to-premises transfer application with the California Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control after the CUA is approved or in parallel if the CUA hearing date is confirmed. What to say: Submit the ABC-257 transfer application, the signed lease, a copy of the entity formation documents, the seller's permit, a diagram of the premises, and the transfer fee. ABC will investigate the applicant, post a 30-day public notice at the premises, and refer the application to SFPD and San Francisco Planning for review. Planning will issue a zoning sign-off only after the CUA is granted. Prepare a written statement for ABC explaining that the restaurant has operated continuously as a bona fide eating place since 1986 and that the Type 47 license will be used solely in conjunction with meal service. Because census tract 106.00 is over the authorized number of on-sale licenses, ABC may require a public convenience or necessity finding from the city; coordinate with Planning and the Board of Supervisors early if ABC requests one.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Complete RBS (Responsible Beverage Service) training for all alcohol servers and managers and obtain food handler cards and a food safety manager certificate for the staff. What to say: Every alcohol server and manager must complete ABC-approved RBS training within 60 days of hire (AB 1221); register on the ABC RBS Portal and complete an approved course. Every employee who handles food must obtain a California Food Handler Card within 30 days of hire, and the restaurant must have at least one certified food protection manager on staff before DPH issues the permit to operate. Schedule these certifications before the ABC transfer is approved so staff are ready when the license is issued.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Renew or transfer the health permit to operate with San Francisco Department of Public Health under the new entity after the CUA is granted. What to say: If the ownership or entity type is changing, file for a new health permit to operate; if only the license type is changing, coordinate with DPH to update the permit. The existing restaurant already has a health permit on file, and no construction is proposed, so DPH should treat this as a continuation of the existing use. Submit the BAN, the certified food safety manager certificate, proof of workers' compensation insurance, and the menu. DPH may require a pre-opening inspection if the entity or operator is new; schedule this inspection at least two weeks in advance.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Obtain ASCAP and BMI public performance licenses for recorded music before opening. What to say: Federal copyright law requires a blanket performance license to play music publicly, whether recorded or live. Apply online to ASCAP and BMI for annual licenses (formula-based fees, typically $300 to $2,500 each for a restaurant of this size). The licenses are effective immediately upon approval and are separate from the city and state permits.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 120 to 300 days. Estimated government cost: $3,100 to $465,000. Notes: The timeline of 120 to 300 days and cost of $3,100 to $465,000 are for approvals granted: the Conditional Use Authorization (120 to 300 days from filing to approval, $3,100 to $15,000 depending on construction cost, per the catalog and comparable CUA filings in North Beach), the ABC Type 47 premises-to-premises transfer (90 to 240 days including escrow, posting, ABC investigation, and city referrals; $17,000 to $450,000 for the license purchase on the open market plus $1,000 to $1,600 in ABC fees), and the health permit to operate (14 to 45 days, $470 to $1,000). The CUA is the critical path: comparable CUA filings at 1318 Grant (2015-000635CUA) took 159 days from filing to approval. ABC transfer timelines depend on undue-concentration review; if ABC requires a public convenience or necessity finding from the Board of Supervisors, add 60 to 120 days to the ABC timeline. The cost range reflects the Type 47 license purchase price, which dominates the total; the applicant should confirm current market prices through an ABC broker before committing to the lease. These figures do not include denial or withdrawal; the nine comparable approvals in the precedent set took 9 to 159 days, all approved. Business registration, entity formation, seller's permit, RBS training, food handler cards, food safety manager certification, and music licenses add 1 to 35 days and $635 to $3,385 in fees, but those are not entitlement approvals and are handled in parallel.
